record.title: TLV320AIC3104 codec reflowed onto the Robot HAT: I2C control at 0x18 on I2C3, I2S3 audio, three supply domains the HAT feeds from rails nobody has published

requires.name: GND
requires.quote: AVDD, DRVDD1/2(1) | Analog supply voltage | 2.7 | 3.3 | 3.6 | V
requires.cite: chips[tlv320aic3104].supplies[0].cite (§8.3 Recommended Operating Conditions, p.7) — the return for the supplies below; the sheet states no separate ground row

requires.name: AVDD
requires.current_from_basis: chips[tlv320aic3104].current_mA.typical is null with its reason: the sheet gives per-mode 'no signal' rows (4.9 mA IDRVDD+IAVDD playback to lineout, p.12) and no figure for current into a speaker load, so this need's draw is CANNOT DETERMINE by the record's own statement.
requires.quote: AVDD, DRVDD1/2(1) | Analog supply voltage | 2.7 | 3.3 | 3.6 | V
requires.cite: chips[tlv320aic3104].supplies[0].cite (§8.3 p.7; pins AVDD 25, DRVDD 18 and 24, Table 7-1 p.5)
requires.note: AVDD and DRVDD1/2 are ONE need here because the sheet gives them one row and one band; the pinout has them on three pins (25, 18, 24). Which HAT rail feeds them is CANNOT DETERMINE (chips[tlv320aic3104].unknowns[1]).

requires.name: DVDD
requires.current_from_basis: the sheet's IDVDD rows (2.3 mA playback, 2.45 mA record, p.12 — chips[tlv320aic3104].current_mA.typical_basis) are per mode and the chip record records no single typical; carried as null rather than picked.
requires.quote: DVDD(1) | Digital core supply voltage | 1.525 | 1.8 | 1.95 | V
requires.note: A 1.8 V-class domain. The HAT must carry a regulator for it or take it from the Radxa — neither is published (chips[tlv320aic3104].unknowns[1]).

requires.name: IOVDD
requires.current_from_basis: no IOVDD current row was transcribed into the chip record; null, not zero.
requires.quote: IOVDD(1) | Digital I/O supply voltage | 1.1 | 1.8 | 3.6 | V
requires.note: Sets the I2C/I2S thresholds. 3.3 V is inside the band, so the RK3566's 3.3 V I2C3/I2S3 needs no level shift IF the HAT feeds IOVDD 3.3 V — which rail it uses is CANNOT DETERMINE (supplies[2].cite).

requires.address_quote: The TLV320AIC3104 responds to the I2C address of 001 1000.
requires.address_cite: chips[tlv320aic3104].i2c_address (§10.5.1 I2C Control Interface, p.45); 001 1000b = 0x18 is arithmetic, and it matches the overlay's `codec@18` / `reg = <0x18>` (research/raw/deploy_audio_aic3104-i2c3.dts)
requires.quote: The TLV320AIC3104 supports the I2C control protocol using 7-bit addressing and is capable of both standard and fast modes.

The device can accept an MCLK input from 512 kHz to 50 MHz, which can then be passed through either a programmable divider or a PLL to get the proper internal audio master clock required by the device. The BCLK input can also be used to generate the internal audio master clock.
requires.cite: chips[tlv320aic3104].mclk (§10.x Audio Clock Generation, p.26); pins MCLK 1, WCLK 3 (chips[tlv320aic3104].pinout — BCLK/DIN/DOUT pin numbers were not transcribed there and are not invented here)
requires.note: The codec is the I2S TARGET (slave): the overlay makes the RK3566's i2s3_2ch bit-clock and frame master (research/raw/deploy_audio_aic3104-i2c3.dts: 'simple-audio-card,bitclock-master = <&pihat_cpu_dai>', 'simple-audio-card,frame-master = <&pihat_cpu_dai>'), sysclk 12.288 MHz ('system-clock-frequency = <12288000>'), MCLK a 12 MHz 'fixed-clock' ('clock-frequency = <12000000>'). MCLK's origin on the HAT is CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §7).

provides.name: LEFT_LOP
provides.basis: Line output, left positive. Whether it reaches the speaker directly or through an amplifier on the HAT is CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §7); listed so a design can join it, never joined here by default.

provides.name: MICBIAS
provides.nominal_v_basis: pin 15 MICBIAS (chips[tlv320aic3104].pinout). The programmed level is not transcribed in the chip record and the HAT's setting is unpublished — null, with this reason.

uncertainties: Which HAT rail feeds AVDD/DRVDD (2.7–3.6 V), DVDD (1.525–1.95 V) and IOVDD (1.1–3.6 V): CANNOT DETERMINE — three domains means the HAT carries at least one 1.8 V regulator or uses the Radxa's; neither is published (chips[tlv320aic3104].unknowns).
Which physical input the microphone uses: the community's 'Mic3R' is not a pin of this device (chips[tlv320aic3104].unknowns[0]); the HAT schematic settles it.
Speaker drive: line out vs an amplifier on the HAT is CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §7).
record.note: Written 2026-09-02 (netlist lane, GOAL.md rung 4) so the codec can sit on the I2C3 netlist beside the BMI088 (0x19/0x68) and the ToF (0x29) and the duplicate-address rule can be asked over all four. Every figure is the chip record's own quote; nothing was re-read from the PDF here. `$from: parts.json` is the shelf's marker for a record the design catalogue admits (cecad.netlist.Design._build_catalogue reads it), the same marker part:xl330-m288-t and part:aht20_soldered carry.
